tooltip.simpleradio_directional.mount: Attach to a vertical antenna with antenna above it. Requires a clear 3×3 area.
tooltip.simpleradio_directional.pattern: Receive only: full directional boost through ±30°; half at ±45°; none at ±60°.
tooltip.simpleradio_directional.aim: Empty-hand click: turn 15° clockwise. Sneak-click: turn back. Stops at ±45°.
tooltip.simpleradio_directional.wide_pat: Receive only: 66% of full directional boost through ±45°; 44% at ±60°; 22% at ±75°; none at ±90°.
handbook.simpleradio_directional.directi:
Directional Receivers adds two receiver arrays that attach to an existing tower's mast to improve reception.

Attach one to a vertical mast with another antenna above it, and point it toward incoming signals. With a suitable tower, even a weak transceiver signal can be picked up over 3,000 blocks away.

Leave its 3x3 mounting area clear. Empty-hand right-click turns the receiver 15 degrees; sneak-right-click turns it back. It can turn up to 45 degrees either way.

Parabolic Receiver:
Full directional reception boost through 30 degrees.
50% of that boost at 45 degrees.
No extra boost at 60 degrees.

Angles are measured to either side of the direction the receiver is aimed. The boost fades smoothly between these values.

Wide-angle Receiver:
66% of the full directional boost through 45 degrees.
44% at 60 degrees.
22% at 75 degrees.
No extra boost at 90 degrees.

Reception outside the directed beam is unaffected. Overlapping receiver bonuses do not combine; the strongest bonus is used.

Directional Receivers improve reception. They do not increase outgoing transmission power.
